$comment: Manifest for Rule B (README/docs numeric sync). Each check declares HOW to compute the true value (source) and one anchor per README file (regex, first-match) to extract the value the doc currently claims. check_docs_sync.py normalizes both sides before comparing. Types: code_constant, json_field, aggregation, manual_external (skipped by the checker, listed for completeness/audit only).

Static shields.io badge text '464 passing' — hardcoded string in the badge URL, NOT generated by CI. True value must come from a real pytest run, which this checker cannot do inside a docs-sync job without also running the full suite (that is the test job's responsibility). Listed here for audit visibility; not automatically checked against the badge text by this script. Recommended: docs-sync job asserts the badge text matches an environment variable passed in from the test job's own pytest summary, once such wiring exists (see Section on CI architecture in pravilo_b_dokumentaciya_final.md).
Judge/human agreement rate on the calibration sample
checks.note: Anchor pinned to the '(30/30)' denominator specifically (n=30 calibration sample, matching TPR k=22/n=22 + TNR k=8/n=8 = 30 in calibration_summary.json) to disambiguate from the adjacent judge-vs-deterministic row in the same table, which reads '...% agreement (28/30)' one line above and would otherwise be matched by an unanchored regex (confirmed the hard way: an earlier version of this anchor without '(30/30)' matched the fractional digit after the decimal point in that other row's '93.3%').

checks.description: Whole-object comparison of the 'overall' error-attribution category counts (generation_failure_candidate/success/reranking_failure/retrieval_failure) — compared field-by-field via 'components' rather than one regex, since no single line in the README states all four numbers as one machine-matchable token; each category IS its own table row, with the category name left untranslated at the start of the row in all three README files, e.g. ru: '| success (gold-документ дошёл до топ-5, ответ верный) | 186 | 74.4% |'.

Join agent_results.jsonl and baseline_results.jsonl on question_id; compare success vs judge_correct. README states the two systems reached an identical success rate on the n=30 sample ('23/30 each') — checked as two components (agent's own count, baseline's own count) that must both equal the value in that sentence. The README does not state the discordant-pair count as a bare number (it appears in the McNemar CI/p-value instead), so that part is not wired to a regex — computed and available in the checker's own output for a human to cross-check, not silently guessed into an anchor.
~$0.016 per question — computed from external, time-varying provider prices; README itself notes this is a calculation, not a measurement
Comparison to Akarsu et al. — requires methodology/currency judgment, not numeric comparison
Comparison to FinAgent-RAG — paper was withdrawn by its author; README notes this explicitly; not a numeric check

pool_sweep_summary.json carries its own 'provenance' field stating it was manually transcribed from a Colab notebook with no recoverable raw per-question data. This check can only ever validate 'README matches the recorded summary JSON', never 'summary JSON matches raw data' — do not report the same confidence level as aggregation-type checks.

CUAD section 'n=5 refusals... unjustified' — the fact '5/5 refused' is checkable, but the qualitative judgment 'unjustified' is not; keep these as separate manifest entries if the numeric half is ever wired up
